relevance_note: Single-patient case report describing a girl with a TNFAIP3 variant: 'a heterozygous variant of uncertain significance in TNFAIP3' (c.2199C>A, p.(Cys733*)), co-occurring with a RAD21 variant.
method_note: Read the whole paper (text, figure legends, abbreviations table, references; the Supplementary material sections contain only a placeholder heading with no converted content). Values were chosen by reading; a short Python script in my scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans and fields. No patient table to transcribe. Label 'patient' by rule 5: single unnamed patient of a case report (the paper calls her 'the proband' or 'the patient', with no identifier). Relatives: 'with a maternal history of cleft palate' and 'born from a vanishing twin pregnancy' were not given rows (mother not tested and not described with HA20 features; unclear whether the mother herself or the maternal family is meant). RAD21 variant recorded as a variant in another gene, attributed unambiguously to the patient. Contradictions and oddities in the paper: (1) Figure 2 and Figure 3 legends call both variants 'de novo', but no parental testing is reported anywhere, so inheritance is 'not reported'. (2) RAD21 transcript printed as NM_006265.2 and NM_006265.1 in the same sentence. (3) RAD21 location printed as chr8:10,673,499–10,658,686 in text and as chromosome 8: position 116,852,561 (GRCh38/hg38) in the Figure 2 legend; Methods say the UCSC browser used GRCh37/hg19, while both figure legends give GRCh38/hg38 positions. (4) Text says each variant 'causes change on the Glycine amino acid with termination codon', contradicting p.(Cys733*) and p.(Gln436*). (5) RAD21 classification given as 'likely pathogenic', 'probably pathogenic' and 'pathogenic for CdLS type 4'; the abstract calls it 'novel' while the Discussion says it is in ClinVar as pathogenic. (6) The upper-limb reduction defect wording in the Results exam repeats the Introduction's general CdLS description verbatim, and the Methods exam omits limb findings; recorded as observed because it is stated for the patient, but it may be boilerplate. (7) A first skin biopsy at a local center was 'compatible with pemphigus foliaceus'; the later biopsy confirmed pustular psoriasis, which is what is recorded. Other choices: authors do not diagnose HA20 (TNFAIP3 variant is a VUS; disease label records CdLS plus generalized pustular psoriasis). Only in silico evidence (AlphaFold modelling, UniProt Variant Viewer) is given for either variant; the GEO analysis concerns RAD21 knockdown, not this variant, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Age at onset not recorded: the paper gives an '8-month history' at age 13, not an onset age; kept in severity_or_detail of the plaques row. Dysprosody and limited social interaction ('Neurocognitive features') are recorded as features, but the checklist item 'central nervous system involvement' is left 'not reported' because the paper does not state CNS involvement. Growth failure checklist item marked observed from short stature and low weight-for-age.
